description:
Hello everyone!

We are a team of students interested in science, technology, space, and innovation. Our goal is to learn new things, share ideas, and find simple solutions to real-world problems.

We welcome students who are interested in programming, designing, engineering, research, and creative thinking.

No special experience is required. Interest, teamwork, creativity, and willingness to learn are enough.

Let's work together, share our knowledge, and turn our ideas into reality!
summary: MARS REGEN is a NASA-inspired student project focused on sustainable space exploration. Its main goal is to reduce space waste by identifying, collecting, and recycling useful materials from inactive satellites and discarded space components. The recovered materials can be processed and reused to manufacture new satellite and rover parts at a Mars research base. By promoting material recovery and reuse, MARS REGEN aims to support cleaner orbital environments, reduce space debris, and encourage responsible use of resources. Our vision is to build a safer, cleaner, and more sustainable future for space exploration.
details:
MARS REGEN – Mars Exploration & Satellite Recycling Simulator

MARS REGEN is an interactive educational simulation game designed to demonstrate the future of Mars exploration and sustainable space technology. The project allows players to experience the complete process of planning, designing, manufacturing, testing, and operating satellites for Mars missions.

The game begins with team selection and mission planning. Players select satellite materials, components, weight, and estimated manufacturing costs. They then build and test the satellite, identify technical faults, and prepare it for launch from Earth to Mars.

During the Mars exploration stage, players monitor important environmental conditions such as temperature, atmosphere, water availability, and dust storms. They can also control exploration vehicles and drones to understand the challenges of operating on Mars.

Another important feature is the Space Debris Recycling System. Players track old satellites and space debris, capture reusable materials, and recycle them to manufacture new satellites. This demonstrates how space technology can become more sustainable and cost-effective.

The main benefits of this project are improving engineering knowledge, encouraging innovation, reducing space debris through recycling concepts, and teaching students about satellite technology and planetary exploration.

The intended impact is to promote sustainable space exploration, inspire young engineers, and demonstrate how reusable materials can support future space missions.

The project was developed as an interactive web-based simulation using Lovable. AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT were used for research assistance, content development, and prompt preparation. Kling AI was used for AI-assisted video creation. The project focuses on a creative combination of space exploration, satellite manufacturing, mission simulation, and space debris recycling in an educational gaming environment.

Our team considered technical feasibility, educational value, mission safety, material selection, manufacturing cost, sustainability, user interaction, and the future possibilities of space exploration.
